goal.en: By the end, you'll know what Instrument-Assisted Soft-Tissue Mobilization (IASTM) is, when it's safe and useful, how to apply it step by step — and how to prove it worked. (3 checks along the way.)
goal.ur: End tak aap jaan jayenge ke Instrument-Assisted Soft-Tissue Mobilization (IASTM) kya hai, kab safe aur faida-mand hai, qadam ba qadam kaise apply hoti hai — aur kaise prove karein ke kaam kiya. (Raste mein 3 checks.)

text.en: Instrument-Assisted Soft-Tissue Mobilization (IASTM) uses tools (stainless steel or similar) to scan tissue and apply controlled strokes. It is used for tendon, muscle and scar tissue restrictions, with a lubricant.
text.ur: Rigid instrument ka istemal karke soft tissue par controlled pressure aur gliding di jati hai, aam tor par active rehabilitation ke sath adjunct ke taur par.

simpler.en: Using a smooth hand-held tool to stroke and press the soft tissue to find tight areas and improve movement.
simpler.ur: IASTM mein ek rigid instrument se soft tissue par controlled pressure aur gliding ki jati hai.

text.en: Like running a smooth spoon over a bumpy surface: the tool lets you feel and treat irregularities with less effort on your hands.
text.ur: Jaise ubhri hui surface par chikna chamach pherna: tool aap ko be-qaidgiyan mehsoos karne aur un par kaam karne deta hai, aur aap ke hands par kam zor parta hai.

text.en:
Three ideas carry this whole technique:
**1.** The tool is a way to scan and apply force, not a reason to push harder.
**2.** Light strokes first; bruising is not the goal.
**3.** Pair with movement and loading afterward.
text.ur: Sensory aur mechanical loading ke zariye pain aur range mein short-term tabdeeli aa sakti hai. Skin ka laal hona ya petechiae nazar aana effectiveness ke liye zaroori nahi. Tissue ko jaan-boojh kar bruise karna therapeutic goal nahi aur evidence isay support nahi karta.

question.ur: Pehle vocabulary — clinicians yeh lafz bohat use karte hain. **Scanning** ka matlab kya hai?

text.en:
So when does **Instrument-Assisted Soft-Tissue Mobilization (IASTM)** make sense?
• Persistent tendon or muscle tightness where hands-on soft-tissue work is suitable.
• As an adjunct before exercise.
text.ur: Adjunct ke taur par soft-tissue pain ya stiffness; loading se pehle warm-up.

text.en:
And just as important — when you should NOT use it, or should stop:
• Open wounds, skin disease, infection, deep vein thrombosis or fragile skin.
• Blood-thinning medication or bleeding disorders, unless checked with a doctor.
• Severe osteoporosis in the area or recent surgery.
text.ur:
Anticoagulation, nazuk skin, neuropathy ya varicosities.
Khula zakhm, active infection, uncontrolled bleeding disorder, DVT ka shak ya acute hematoma.
Bruising ko effectiveness ka marker samajhna, skin damage karna, aur bleeding risk ya skin problems ignore karna avoid karein. Treatment ke dauran pain, skin response aur symptoms monitor karein; unusual response par stop karein.

title.en: How to do it — 6 steps, each with its reason
title.ur: Kaise karein — 6 qadam, har ek ki wajah ke saath

steps.title: Assess and explain
steps.detail: Check skin and tissue and explain what the patient will feel.

steps.title: Apply lubricant
steps.detail: Use enough so the tool glides.

steps.title: Scan lightly
steps.detail: Stroke along the area to find tight, rough or tender spots.

steps.title: Treat with controlled strokes
steps.detail: Use short, repeated strokes at 30-60 degrees along or across the tissue.

steps.title: Monitor skin and pain
steps.detail: Reduce pressure if skin reddens strongly or pain is sharp.

beats.ur:
1. Skin, circulation, sensation aur bleeding risk ki screening karein.
2. Instrument ka edge aur angle aisa choose karein ke contact controlled rahe.
3. Relevant region par light-to-moderate strokes apply karein.
4. Dose ko symptoms ke response ke mutabiq rakhein.
5. Active mobility ya loading follow karein.

question.en: Imagine the patient is in front of you. What do you do FIRST?
question.ur: Farz karein patient aap ke saamne hai. Aap SAB SE PEHLE kya karenge?

text.en: How much? Typical teaching range: 1-3 minutes per area, light to moderate pressure, usually not more than 2 sessions per week for the same area, followed by exercise.
text.ur: Aksar ek region par 30 seconds se kuch minutes tak. Bar bar aggressive passes se bachein jo bruising ya lambi soreness paida karein.

beats.patient: Yusuf, 46, tight Achilles area after training, pain with calf raises.
beats.assessment: Tenderness in the calf and tendon, no tear signs.
beats.treatment: You scan, then stroke the calf for two minutes with a tool, avoiding the skin turning sore.
beats.reassess: Calf raises feel easier. A progressive loading plan is the main treatment.
beats.ur:
Ek misal se poora clinical flow dekhein:
Farz karein patient ko calf movement mein stiffness mehsoos hoti hai. Screening ke baad clinician controlled instrument strokes ka short trial karta hai aur phir movement dobara check karta hai. Bruising paida karna maqsad nahi. Yeh illustrative example hai.

text.en:
The mistakes I see most often:
• Believing bruising means it worked.
• Pressing hard without lubricant.
• Using the tool without an exercise plan.
text.ur:
Sab se aam ghaltiyan:
• Believing bruising means it worked.
• Pressing hard without lubricant.
• Using the tool without an exercise plan.

answer.en: No. They are not the goal.

text.en: Small trials show possible short-term improvements in pain and range. Evidence quality is low and benefits are not clearly greater than other soft-tissue methods.
text.ur: IASTM ke benefits condition aur outcome ke mutabiq mixed ho sakte hain. Session ke baad functional change assess karein aur bruising ko treatment success ka proof na kahein.
